grammar.topic: must have / might have / can't have + V3 (past deduction)
explainTr: Geçmişte ne olduğunu tahmin etmek için üç kalıp kullanırız. Neredeyse eminsek: must have + V3 (He must have lost it.). Emin değilsek: might / could have + V3 (She might have left it.).
Olması imkânsız görünüyorsa: can't have + V3 (He can't have taken it; he was in class.). 'Mustn't have' kullanma, yanlıştır.
Hepsinde 'have' sabit, ana fiil üçüncü halde (V3). Çıkarım için bir ipucu (clue) olması iyi bir alışkanlıktır.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'almış olmalı / almış olabilir / almış olamaz' ekle yapılır. İngilizcede 'have + V3' sabit, başa must / might / can't gelir.

examples.tr: Çantayı almış olamaz; bütün gün benimleydi.

reading.title: The case of the missing laptop
reading.text:
On Monday morning, Mr. Brown's office was busier than usual. A teacher named Mr. Reed rushed in with a worried face. "My laptop has vanished!" he said. "I left it on my desk on Friday, and now it's gone."

Hafsa, who was helping at the front office that day, listened carefully. "Could someone have borrowed it?" she asked. Mr. Reed shook his head. "It can't have been a student. The classroom was locked all weekend."

"Then maybe the cleaning staff moved it," suggested Mr. Brown. He called the janitor, Mr. Ortiz, who explained that he had cleaned the room on Saturday and had not touched any computers. "Honestly, I might have moved some papers, but I would never take a laptop," he said.

Hafsa began to search for clues. She asked Mr. Reed, "When did you last see it?" He thought for a moment. "On Friday, after the last class. I was in a hurry because I had a dentist appointment." Hafsa nodded. "Then you must have taken it with you, or you might have put it somewhere else."

Mr. Reed frowned. "I can't have taken it. I only had my small bag." Still, Hafsa asked him to check the car. Ten minutes later, he came back, red in the face. The laptop was on the back seat. "I must have put it there when I grabbed my coat," he said.

Everyone laughed with relief. Mr. Brown said, "It's obvious we all jumped to conclusions. Without real evidence, nobody should suspect anyone." Hafsa smiled. "In my country we say the lost thing is always in the last place you look."

At the end of the day, Mr. Brown handed Hafsa a small card. It said: "Lost and Found: Please label your belongings!" "This is for the school hallway," he explained. "Could you help me hang it near the lockers?" Hafsa happily agreed. She had been a detective for one morning, and she had enjoyed every minute of it.

writing.promptTr: Bir kayıp eşya hikâyesi yaz (ör. kayıp çanta, anahtar, cüzdan). Ne olmuş olabileceğine dair çıkarımlarını must have, might have, can't have ile anlat. 120-180 kelime.
writing.promptEn: Write a short story about a lost item at school. Use must have, might have and can't have to guess what happened (120-180 words).
frames: It might have ... , but it can't have ...
In the end, we found it ...
writing.model: Yesterday, a student's backpack disappeared from the hallway near the lockers. The student, Ben, was very upset because his homework was inside. We began to search for clues. First, we thought someone might have taken it by mistake, because many backpacks look the same. However, Ben's bag is bright green with a big yellow tag, so a classmate can't have confused it with another one. Then we asked the janitor, Mr. Ortiz. He said he had cleaned the hallway at four o'clock, and he must have moved the bag when he mopped the floor. We checked the janitor's closet, and the backpack was there, under a bucket. It's obvious that nobody tried to steal it. Ben was relieved and thanked everybody. Now the school will put a small box in the hallway for lost belongings. I think this is a good idea, and I'm happy that we solved the mystery without blaming anyone.
checklistTr: Must have, might have ve can't have'in üçünü de kullandın mı?
Her çıkarımın arkasında bir neden (ipucu) var mı?
Must have + V3 yapısında fiili üçüncü hale (V3) koydun mu?
